<finding task="0"><quote>So after the change merges, a worktree on a branch that lacks those files inherits the main checkout's freeze date and interpreter, with no sign of it.</quote><plan>Every task's requirements include this section.</plan><fix>Add the required `## Review Focus` section between Global Constraints and Decisions. It is missing entirely. List the five uncovered failure modes most likely to bite a person, most likely first: nested-worktree inheritance; a user run of a skill script through the `~/.claude/skills` symlink floating within its floors; `notice.sh` or the pre-commit hook run from outside the repo; a bump that leaves a gate's stack unresolvable; a citation split across markup or a line break. Then add a test for each line in the task whose code the person would see fail.</fix></finding>
<finding task="0"><quote>| D1 | How the checks choose versions | Exact pins in one file, plus a separate drift run on the newest releases. Not a floating gate |</quote><plan>**D1 to D8** are the owner decisions in the spec's table "Decisions (owner, 2026-10-21)".</plan><fix>The plan's `## Decisions` entries reuse D1–D8 for its own plan-review decisions, so every "D2" or "D4" reference is ambiguous. Number the plan's decisions from D9 (or use another prefix). Fix "Spec-level decisions (D1, D2, D6)" to list every decision that changes spec text, including the floors rule (see the Task 9 finding).</fix></finding>
<finding task="0"><quote>**Plan 63.** It edits `build/run_commit_lints.sh`. This work lands after plan 63, or the plan that lands second rebases onto the other and re-reads the anchors.</quote><plan>It does not edit `build/run_commit_lints.sh`. It only runs it, so there is no textual conflict in that file.</plan><fix>Keep the spec's ordering rule. Give Task 14 a first step that fetches main, checks whether plan 63 has landed, and re-reads the `run_commit_lints.sh` anchors before editing. If the plan's finding that plan 63 does not touch the file is right, raise it with the owner as a spec correction rather than overriding the spec silently.</fix></finding>

Add an amendment step in Task 9 that replaces R4.1.4's "must match" sentence with the at-most rule, tagged `(owner, plan 66, 2026-10-21)`. Log D4 as "Task 9 (spec amendment)".</fix></finding>

<finding task="11"><quote>The known stale citations are the Polars, Altair and plotly lines, `skills/bayesian-workflow/references/model-comparison.md:130`, `references/model-criticism.md:196` and `skills/deep-learning/references/frameworks.md:94-95`.</quote><plan>| `recommend-visualization` `'Polars 1.42'`, five places | 8 |</plan><fix>`[cited]` keeps `altair = '6.2'` and `plotly = '6.8'`, and `bump` never moves `[cited]`. Add a step that settles them under R6.5: either re-check and update both the text and `[cited]`, or log a deferred item that says they were verified on 6.2 and 6.8, not re-checked on 6.3.0 and 7.1.0.</fix></finding>
